help.title: Aiuto e numeri di emergenza
help.subtitle: Non sei solo/a. Trova supporto immediato qui.
help.meta_description: Linee di crisi e servizi di supporto LGBTQIA+ gratuiti e anonimi in tutto il mondo. Non sei solo/a.
help.emergency_body: Chiama subito i servizi di emergenza: 112 (UE) o 911 (US/CA). Ogni secondo conta.
help.disclaimer: Queer Guide non sostituisce l'aiuto professionale.
help.no_results: Nessun numero corrisponde a questi filtri. Prova "Tutti i paesi" o consulta le directory internazionali.
help.error_body: In caso di pericolo immediato, chiama il numero di emergenza locale: 112 (UE) o 911 (US/CA).
help.reveal_aria: Clicca in un punto qualsiasi per rivedere la pagina
help.hidden_hint: Pagina nascosta. Clicca ovunque per rivederla.
help.expect_1: You'll hear a short greeting. You don't have to give your name.
help.expect_2: You can hang up at any time. You can call back as often as you need.
help.expect_3: Free hotlines in DE/AT/CH don't appear on itemized phone bills.
help.expect_4: If you can't speak, ask for text or chat — most hotlines offer it.
help.self_help_trigger: Non te la senti di parlare?
help.self_help_desc: Short techniques you can use while you wait, or instead of a call if you're not ready.
help.breathing_1: Breathe in through your nose for 4 seconds.
help.breathing_3: Breathe out through your mouth for 8 seconds.
help.grounding_intro: Name, out loud or in your head:
help.safety_plan_desc: A short written plan you can pull up when things get bad — your warning signs, coping steps, people to call, and reasons to live.
help.report_aria: Report a problem with this hotline
help.report_desc: Thanks for helping keep this list accurate. Reports are reviewed by our team.
help.closed_no_alt: Questa linea è chiusa in questo momento e non abbiamo altre linee aperte per questo paese. In caso di pericolo immediato, usa il numero di emergenza qui sopra.
help.directories_subtitle: Sono elenchi e organizzazioni di riferimento: siti web, non linee telefoniche dirette.
help.helping_body: Se stai ascoltando qualcuno in crisi: restagli accanto, prendi sul serio ciò che dice e non lasciarlo solo. Non devi avere le risposte. Chiamate insieme una linea, oppure chiama tu per chiedere cosa fare.
help.know_the_law_body: Se sia sicuro vivere apertamente, cercare assistenza sanitaria o denunciare un reato dipende da dove ti trovi. Verifica la situazione legale prima di agire.
help.link_unavailable: Sito al momento non raggiungibile: nuova verifica in corso.
help.no_country_body: Scegli un paese qui sopra e ti mostreremo la linea migliore. Tutte le linee sono elencate sotto.
help.no_country_title: Non siamo riusciti a capire dove ti trovi
help.no_lines_body: Se sei in pericolo adesso, chiama i soccorsi: 112 (UE) o 911 (USA/CA).
help.no_police_policy: Questa linea dichiara di non contattare mai la polizia o i servizi di emergenza senza una tua richiesta esplicita.
help.org_coverage: Questo elenco è tutt'altro che completo. Se manca un gruppo di cui ti fidi, segnalacelo. Un risultato vuoto significa che non ne abbiamo notizia, non che non esista aiuto.
help.phone_only: Solo telefonicamente, secondo i nostri dati.
help.phone_only_with_site: Solo telefonicamente, secondo i nostri dati. Il loro sito potrebbe offrire chat o email.
help.reports_police_warning: Questa linea può contattare la polizia o i servizi di emergenza senza il tuo consenso.
help.scope_all: Linee da tutti i paesi registrati.
help.scope_dialog_desc: Le linee sono ordinate per paese servito. Gli elenchi internazionali restano visibili qualunque sia la scelta.
help.support_orgs_body: Centri comunitari e associazioni che offrono supporto di persona.

sections.sameYearNote: [IT] What was happening in other countries the same year.

hidden-lives.title: [IT] Hidden lives
hidden-lives.intro: [IT] Before 1800, queer life survived in the shadows of law and church. What the record preserves is mostly persecution — trials, executions, edicts — alongside rare glimpses of love and community that outlasted them.

empire-criminalization.title: [IT] Empire & criminalization
empire-criminalization.intro: [IT] Colonial empires exported sodomy laws across the globe in the 19th century, while a few states — revolutionary France first among them — quietly removed their own. Much of today's legal map was drawn in this era.

birth-of-movement.title: [IT] Birth of a movement
birth-of-movement.intro: [IT] Between the 1860s and the early 1930s the first words, organizations and campaigns emerged: Kertbeny coined 'homosexual', Hirschfeld founded the first gay rights organization, and Berlin briefly became the queer capital of the world.

destruction.title: [IT] Destruction
destruction.intro: [IT] Fascism destroyed the first movement. The Nazis burned Hirschfeld's institute, tightened Paragraph 175 and deported thousands of gay men to concentration camps. Remembering this era is part of why this timeline exists.

homophile-years.title: [IT] The homophile years
homophile-years.intro: [IT] After the war, small 'homophile' groups rebuilt quietly — Mattachine, the Daughters of Bilitis, Arcadie, the COC — trading radicalism for respectability while police raids and purges continued.

liberation.title: [IT] Liberation
liberation.intro: [IT] Stonewall in 1969 turned decades of quiet organizing into open revolt. Pride marches spread worldwide, homosexuality left the psychiatric manuals, and the first anti-discrimination laws were won.

aids-crisis.title: [IT] The AIDS crisis
aids-crisis.intro: [IT] A generation was decimated while governments looked away. The epidemic's grief forged the militant activism — ACT UP, treatment-access campaigns — that reshaped medicine and queer politics alike.

recognition.title: [IT] Recognition
recognition.intro: [IT] From the first registered partnerships to the Netherlands opening marriage in 2001, courts and parliaments began recognizing queer lives: decriminalization accelerated and trans rights entered the legal mainstream.

equality-wave.title: [IT] The equality wave
equality-wave.intro: [IT] The 2010s brought marriage equality to dozens of countries on every continent, landmark court rulings from the United States to India, and unprecedented queer visibility in public life.

backlash-now.title: [IT] Backlash & now
backlash-now.intro: [IT] Progress continues — and so does organized backlash: 'LGBT-free zones', anti-trans legislation and new criminalization drives. The timeline is still being written.

sources.title: [IT] Where this data comes from
sources.lede: [IT] We publish the legal status of LGBTQ+ people in every country and territory we cover. This page says who recorded it, how often we refresh it, how much of it we actually hold, and the questions it cannot answer.
sources.metaTitle: [IT] Where our LGBTQ+ rights data comes from
sources.metaDescription: [IT] The sources, refresh cadence, coverage and known limits behind the legal status we publish for every country and territory.

section.limits: [IT] What this data cannot tell you

kicker.score: [IT] How it is built, and what it hides

coverage.status: [IT] Countries with a recorded legal status

body.source: [IT] Every legal status on this site — criminalisation, partnership recognition, anti-discrimination protection, gender recognition, conversion therapy and intersex bodily integrity — comes from the ILGA World Database, the reference dataset maintained by the International Lesbian, Gay, Bisexual, Trans and Intersex Association.
body.refresh: [IT] We re-import it nightly. Where a country page shows an "Updated" date, that is the date ILGA last revised that record, not the date we fetched it.
body.unscored: [IT] The unscored rows are uninhabited or near-uninhabited territories with no ILGA entry. We list them as "not scored" rather than giving them a default, because a default would read as a measurement.
body.scoreHow: [IT] The score runs 0–100. It starts at 50 and moves up or down as each recorded right is added: decriminalisation and marriage weigh heaviest, then anti-discrimination protections, hate-crime law, adoption, legal gender recognition and a conversion-therapy ban.
body.scoreLimit: [IT] Because it opens at 50 and adds from there, a country we hold almost nothing about lands mid-scale rather than reading as unknown. A middling score can mean middling rights or thin data, and the number cannot tell you which.
body.scoreLens: [IT] It is also a single number for very different lives. Protections are recorded separately for sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression and sex characteristics, and those four rarely move together — a country can protect sexual orientation thoroughly and gender identity not at all. Read the per-right breakdown on a country page rather than the score alone.
body.scoreNotSafety: [IT] The score describes law on paper. It is not a safety rating, and it says nothing about enforcement, policing or how welcome you will be made to feel.

limits.national: [IT] It is national. Where rights vary by state or province — the United States, Indonesia, Nigeria, Mexico and others — a single national figure averages that away.
limits.enforcement: [IT] It records statutes, not enforcement. A law that is rarely applied and a law applied constantly look identical here.
limits.trans: [IT] Several facts that matter most to trans travellers are not in this dataset at all: bathroom and facility access, how identity documents are treated at borders, and access to gender-affirming healthcare.
limits.personal: [IT] It knows nothing about you. Your citizenship, residency, gender marker and relationship status all change what applies, and we hold none of them.
limits.corrections: [IT] If something here is wrong, tell us — corrections to the underlying record should also go to ILGA, who maintain it.

story.title: Come è iniziata
story.p1: Trovare un bar queer-friendly non dovrebbe richiedere una chat di gruppo, tre thread di forum e un atto di fede. Abbiamo iniziato Queer Guide perché eravamo stanchi di indovinare quali spazi fossero davvero sicuri — e quali a giugno si limitassero a mettere un arcobaleno sul logo.
story.p2: Una lista personale di posti fidati è diventata una directory globale: verificata dalla comunità, costruita su esperienze vere, gratuita. In viaggio da soli, in trasloco, o solo alla ricerca di un posto dove stare un venerdì sera: si comincia da qui.
